messages:
alex_h: Heads-up — I prototyped a small change to the intake API so model metadata carries an explicit api_version field. Goal is to avoid silent breakages when we change bench wiring or compat checks.

priya_k: Nice. Do you mean a top-level field in the model manifest or an HTTP header?

alex_h: Top-level manifest + header for runtime requests. Example: `api_version: "2"` in model.yaml and `X-Model-API-Version: 2` on the HTTP side.

jamal_r: What's the migration plan? We need to keep old models serving and preserve bench comparators.

alex_h: Plan A: compatibility shim in ingest that maps v1 manifests to v2 normalized fields. Plan B: soft-reject models without api_version after a grace period.

sara_w: Concern — the shim can hide semantic mismatches (e.g., kv-cache layout changes). We should gate the shim with smoke bench runs that assert numerical parity on golden prompts.

jamal_r: Agreed. If shim applied we must run a lightweight bench that checks: top-k logprobs on 20 golden inputs, latency smoke, and kv-cache size estimate. If any metric deviates >2% flag for manual review.

onboard-bot: CI: small-smoke for model `foo-bert` returned +1.8% logprob delta on sample set — flagged. (link: https://ci/redwood/22345)

priya_k: How do we version the bench harness itself? If bench changes, comparisons become noisy.

alex_h: We pin bench harness to a release tag in the manifest (`bench_tag: v2026-03-01`) so each model's smoke uses a stable harness. Later we can re-run full rebaseline jobs to lift tags.

sara_w: That helps. Also propose we include a small deterministic evaluation vector in the manifest (sha256 of test inputs) so we can ensure identical inputs across replays.

jamal_r: For runtime compatibility, we should expose a compatibility matrix API: given model X and target runtime Y it returns supported features (kv-cache, quant profiles, fused-attn). This prevents surprises at routing time.

alex_h: Yeah, Router can query that matrix and pick fallback variants automatically. Implementation idea: compat matrix is generated during ingest and stored as JSON in model registry under `compat/` namespace.

priya_k: Storage format idea — flat keys to keep it simple: `compat.kv_cache: true`, `compat.quant_modes: [q4_q8]`, `compat.seq_len: 2048`. Keep values primitive or arrays only.

sara_w: Tradeoff: flat keys are easy to query but brittle for future nested features. Maybe we accept flat now and reserve `compat.raw` for an opaque JSON blob for extensibility.

jamal_r: Ops question — how long do we keep old bench tags and shim-enabled ingest? We need a deprecation cadence.

alex_h: Proposal: 6 months grace after v2 rollout, then soft-enforce with onboarding warnings, and 12 months before hard-reject. We also email model owners and surface deprecation in Console.

priya_k: Sounds reasonable. Last: telemetry. We should emit a `onboard.api_version` metric and `onboard.shim_used` boolean per model ingest so we can track usage and hot paths.

onboard-bot: Note: created ticket ENGM-4123 to implement compat matrix + bench pinning.

alex_h: Sweet — I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the sample manifest snippet and a tiny shim prototype. Would appreciate quick reviews from @priya_k and @jamal_r. :thumbsup:

priya_k: Happy to review tomorrow morning. :+1:

jamal_r: Same. I want to make sure the smoke thresholds and inputs are easily editable without redeploying the shim.

sara_w: +1 from me. If you want I can draft the Console UX copy for deprecation notices.

alex_h: Thanks all — I'll add a small checklist to the PR describing the canary steps and manual review playbook.
